title: Learner single sign-on (SAML) for your school
description: Let learners sign in with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or Keycloak over SAML 2.0. Set up per school, for learners only.

settings.title: Let learners sign in with *their work accounts*
settings.description: Connect your school to your identity provider so learners use the account they already have. Each school sets up its own connection.
settings.smallPrint: Business plan on the cloud. Included in self-hosted CourseLit.

settings.title: Built for organisations training their people

items.title: One connection per school
items.description: Each school connects its own identity provider. Learners see a Sign in with button on the school's sign-in page.

items.title: Require SSO by email domain
items.description: Verify a domain with a DNS record, then require SSO for it. Other learners keep using email codes or Google.

items.title: Test before you switch on
items.description: Run a test sign-in and see what the provider sent, with a reason code and a fix if it fails.

settings.title: Set it up in the admin
settings.description: The school owner does this under Settings, then Login providers.

items.title: Create the connection
items.description: Name the sign-in button and paste your identity provider's metadata.

items.title: Register CourseLit and verify domains
items.description: Copy the ACS URL and entity ID into your provider, then add a DNS TXT record for each email domain.

items.title: Test, then turn it on
items.description: Run a test sign-in. When it passes, turn the connection on for your learners.

settings.title: For learners only
settings.body:
Single sign-on is for the people who learn on your school's website. Team members always sign in to the admin with an email code or Google, and an account that signs in with SSO never gets team access.

The SSO setup is done by the school owner in the admin. It cannot be done with an API key or an AI assistant.

[How learners sign in](/docs/learners/sign-in)

settings.title: Availability
settings.body:
On the cloud, learner SSO is part of the **Business** plan. Self-hosted CourseLit includes it with every other feature when `BILLING_MODE` is set to `oss`.

[See pricing](/pricing) · [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting/single-sign-on)

items.question: Which identity providers work?
items.answer: Any SAML 2.0 provider. The setup guide shows the field names for Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Keycloak.

items.question: Can my team sign in to the admin with SSO?
items.answer: No. SSO is for learners only. Team members sign in to the admin with an email code or Google.

items.question: What must my identity provider send?
items.answer: A signed assertion using RSA-SHA256 or stronger, a persistent NameID, and the learner's email address.

items.question: Does every learner have to use SSO?
items.answer: Only if you choose. You can require SSO for verified email domains, and learners with other addresses keep their usual sign-in methods.
